pricing_assumptions.title: ⚠️ Pricing Assumptions & Limitations

pricing_assumptions.adversarial: Adversarial comparison costs are NOT tracked. Running dual-model comparisons doubles token usage but only primary model costs appear here.

usage.title: How to Use ClassyMail
usage.step1_desc: The main dashboard provides a real-time view of all incoming and processed emails with live statistics.
usage.step1_li1: Status Codes: Green (Processed), Amber (Review Required), Red (Error), Blue (Processing).
usage.step1_li2: Confidence Scores: 0-100% indicating AI certainty. Scores below 85% trigger human review.
usage.step1_li3: Badges: Look for indicators showing Sensitive Data detected, Images found, or Adversarial comparison enabled.
usage.step1_li4: Processing Time: Hover over the clock icon to see a detailed breakdown (OCR, Classification, PII) for each email.
usage.step2_desc: Click 'Open Details' on any email to enter the full review mode with side-by-side comparison.
usage.step2_li1: View the original PDF alongside the AI-extracted Markdown content.
usage.step2_li2: Inspect the AI Analysis section: detected intents, confidence scores, and reasoning chain.
usage.step2_li3: Correct categories if the AI made an error. Add a reason to feed the fine-tuning loop.
usage.step2_li4: Compare adversarial results when dual-model processing is enabled (Phi-4 vs GPT-4o-mini).
usage.step3_desc: Use the Upload tab to manually ingest PDF files for testing or batch processing.
usage.step3_li1: Drag & drop or browse to select one or multiple PDF files (max 20 MB each).
usage.step3_li2: In production, files arrive automatically via Email integration or direct Blob Storage upload.
usage.step4_desc: Fine-tune the engine behavior in the Settings tab to match your use case.
usage.step4_li1: Categories: Define exact intent names and descriptions. Changes apply immediately to new classifications.
usage.step4_li2: Processing Strategy: Switch between Standard (fast), Reasoning (accurate), or Vision (image-aware) modes.
usage.step4_li3: PII Settings: Enable or disable PII detection, choose the method (LLM, Azure AI Language, or Hybrid), and select the model.

strategies.title: Processing Strategies
strategies.desc: Choose the strategy that best fits your document types. Each strategy optimizes for different trade-offs between speed, accuracy, and cost.
strategies.standard_desc: Fast classification using Phi-4 (under 8K tokens) or GPT-4o-mini (larger documents). Best for text-heavy emails with clear intent. Lowest cost per document.
strategies.reasoning_desc: Forces the AI to output a step-by-step justification before classifying. Improves accuracy on ambiguous or multi-intent emails. Slightly higher latency.
strategies.vision_desc: Enables full image analysis using GPT-4o-mini vision capabilities. Best for documents containing photos, diagrams, or scanned handwriting that affect classification.

ai.title: AI Complexity & Reasoning
ai.desc: The system assesses each email's complexity and adapts its approach:
ai.li1: Multi-Intent Detection: Identifies emails requesting multiple distinct actions (e.g., 'Change address AND send statement') and classifies each intent separately.
ai.li2: Ambiguity Handling: Resolves vague wording by leveraging context from attachments, headers, and document structure.
ai.li3: Reasoning Mode: When enabled, the AI outputs a chain-of-thought justification before classifying, significantly improving accuracy on complex cases.
ai.li4: Token Budget Routing: Documents under 8K tokens are processed by Phi-4 (faster, cheaper); larger documents automatically route to GPT-4o-mini.

privacy.title: Privacy & Data Safety (PII)
privacy.desc: GDPR-compliant Personal Identifiable Information (PII) management with configurable detection and anonymization:
privacy.detection_desc: The AI flags emails containing sensitive data. Enable in Settings > Processing > Email Preprocessing.
privacy.detection_li1: LLM-based: Contextual understanding using your chosen model — extracts names, emails, phones, addresses, contract IDs, and dates.
privacy.detection_li2: Azure AI Language: Native service with 40+ predefined PII categories (~€0.001/email).
privacy.detection_li3: Hybrid: Runs both methods in parallel and merges results for maximum accuracy.
privacy.detection_li4: Configurable Model: PII detection can reuse your classification model (Auto) or use a dedicated deployment (gpt-4o-mini, gpt-5-nano, etc.).
privacy.detection_categories: Detected categories: names, emails, phones, addresses, contract/policy numbers, dates, and other identifiers (SSN, passport, IBAN).
privacy.anonymization_desc: When exporting JSONL data for fine-tuning, the system automatically scrubs all PII using a dedicated anonymizer model:
privacy.anonymization_li1: Names, emails, and dates are replaced with generic placeholders ([Name], [Email], [Date]).
privacy.anonymization_li2: Financial figures, addresses, and reference numbers are masked.
privacy.anonymization_li3: Markdown structure (headers, links, tables) is fully preserved.
privacy.settings_hint: Configure PII detection method and model in Settings > Processing > Email Preprocessing.

vision.title: Smart Vision (Mistral Document AI)
vision.desc: The system leverages Mistral's advanced Layout Analysis to intelligently handle visual content in documents.
vision.standard_desc: The pipeline is 'Content Aware': Text documents are OCR'd normally. However, if visual elements (photos, diagrams) are detected inside the document, they are automatically captioned by the Vision model.
vision.vision_desc: The system intelligently distinguishes between a 'scanned page' (treated as text source) and 'meaningful images' (e.g. car crash photos). Redundant descriptions of the page itself are suppressed.
vision.fallback_desc: Primary OCR uses Mistral Document AI. If Mistral is unavailable or the circuit breaker trips, the system falls back to Azure Document Intelligence via AI Foundry. Mistral handles up to 8 pages; beyond that, GPT-4o-mini provides supplementary image descriptions.

architecture.title: System Architecture
architecture.desc_html: The ClassyMail system leverages Azure Container Apps to host two distinct microservices: the FastAPI Backend (handling API requests) and the Background Worker (processing long-running tasks asynchronously). This decoupling allows independent scaling: the API scales on HTTP traffic, while the Worker scales based on Service Bus queue depth.
